assertions.assertion: Explains that a new public key must be published (available via JWKS as a validation key) BEFORE it is used to sign tokens
assertions.rationale: Step 1 publishes the new key as a validation key first and explains APIs must fetch it from JWKS before it signs, to avoid unknown-kid rejections.

assertions.assertion: Explains that the retired public key must remain available until all tokens signed with it have expired
assertions.rationale: Step 2/3 keep the old key as a validation key until all tokens signed with it expire before removing it.

assertions.assertion: Describes a phased/multi-step rotation using AddSigningCredential and AddValidationKey (or equivalent) rather than a single hard cut-over
assertions.rationale: Gives a three-step sequence using AddSigningCredential and AddValidationKey with wait periods, explicitly not a single swap.

assertions.assertion: Notes that Automatic Key Management handles this overlap automatically while manual key managers must do phased rotation
assertions.rationale: Does not mention Automatic Key Management at all, nor the contrast that it handles the overlap automatically while manual key management requires the phased process.
